title: Psalms Chapter 66 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 66 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 66 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 66.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:1 instruct all the lands to do unto God?
questions.correctAnswer: Make a joyful noise
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:1 says, 'Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands:' instructing all lands to make a joyful noise.

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:2, what should we sing forth?
questions.correctAnswer: The honour of his name
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:2 says, 'Sing forth the honour of his name: make his praise glorious.'

questions.question: In Psalms 66:3, what will happen to God's enemies through the greatness of His power?
options: They shall submit themselves unto Him
questions.correctAnswer: They shall submit themselves unto Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:3 states, 'through the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies submit themselves unto thee.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 66:4 says that only a few people will worship God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:4 says, 'All the earth shall worship thee,' indicating everyone will worship God, not just a few.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:5 invite us to do?
options: Come and see the works of God
questions.correctAnswer: Come and see the works of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:5 says, 'Come and see the works of God,' inviting us to observe His deeds.

questions.question: How did God show His power according to Psalms 66:6?
options: He turned the sea into dry land
He caused the sun to stand still
questions.correctAnswer: He turned the sea into dry land
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:6 states, 'He turned the sea into dry land: they went through the flood on foot.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:7, how long does God rule by His power?
questions.correctAnswer: Forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:7 says, 'He ruleth by his power for ever.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 66:7 says God's eyes do not see the nations.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:7 says, 'his eyes behold the nations,' meaning God sees all nations.

questions.question: What are the people instructed to do in Psalms 66:8?
options: Bless our God and make the voice of His praise to be heard
questions.correctAnswer: Bless our God and make the voice of His praise to be heard
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:8 states, 'O bless our God, ye people, and make the voice of his praise to be heard:'

questions.question: What does God hold according to Psalms 66:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Our soul in life
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:9 says, 'Which holdeth our soul in life, and suffereth not our feet to be moved.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 66:10 compares God's trial of us to the trying of silver.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:10 says, 'thou hast tried us, as silver is tried.'

questions.question: In what order do these events appear in Psalms 66:11-12? 1) Going through fire and water, 2) Being brought into a net, 3) Men riding over our heads, 4) Being brought out into a wealthy place.
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:11-12 states the sequence: 'Thou broughtest us into the net; thou laidst affliction upon our loins. Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place.'

questions.question: What will the psalmist offer in the house of God according to Psalms 66:13-15?
options: Burnt offerings, burnt sacrifices of fatlings, incense of rams, bullocks, and goats
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt offerings, burnt sacrifices of fatlings, incense of rams, bullocks, and goats
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:13-15 mentions burnt offerings and sacrifices of fatlings, rams, bullocks, and goats being offered.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 66:16, the psalmist invites all who fear God to hear what He has done.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:16 says, 'Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what he hath done for my soul.'

questions.question: What must not be regarded in the heart if one wants the Lord to hear their prayers according to Psalms 66:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Iniquity
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:18 says, 'If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 66 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 66 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:8, what are the people instructed to do to God?
options: Bless our God and make the voice of His praise to be heard
Remain silent and meditate on His works
questions.correctAnswer: Bless our God and make the voice of His praise to be heard
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:8 explicitly commands the people to bless God and make the voice of His praise to be heard, emphasizing active praise. This is supported by verses 9 and 10, which describe God's sustaining power and testing of His people, worthy of such praise.

questions.question: How does Psalms 66:9 describe God's care for His people?
options: He holdeth our soul in life and suffers not our feet to be moved
He sends affliction to humble us
He allows us to walk freely without guidance
He tests us like silver is tried
questions.correctAnswer: He holdeth our soul in life and suffers not our feet to be moved
questions.explanation: Verse 9 portrays God's sustaining power by holding the soul in life and preventing the feet from being moved, showing His protection and care. This complements verses 8 and 10 which speak of praising God and His testing of the people.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:10 reveal about the nature of God's testing?
options: God has proved and tried us as silver is tried
questions.correctAnswer: God has proved and tried us as silver is tried
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:10 compares God’s testing of His people to the refining process of silver, indicating a purposeful and purifying trial. This is consistent with verses 9 and 11, which describe God's sustaining care and the afflictions brought upon them.

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:11, what kind of hardships has God allowed His people to experience?
options: He brought them into the net and laid affliction upon their loins
He allowed them to prosper without struggle
He protected them from all trials
questions.correctAnswer: He brought them into the net and laid affliction upon their loins
questions.explanation: Verse 11 describes hardships metaphorically as being caught in a net and suffering affliction on the loins, illustrating the trials God allowed. This complements verses 10 and 12, which speak about testing and overcoming adversity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:12 say about the nature of the trials experienced and God’s deliverance?
options: We went through fire and water, but God brought us into a wealthy place
Trials were minimal and easily overcome
God abandoned us during our trials
We avoided all dangers by our own strength
questions.correctAnswer: We went through fire and water, but God brought us into a wealthy place
questions.explanation: Verse 12 acknowledges severe trials symbolized by fire and water but affirms God's deliverance into a prosperous situation, linking to verses 10 and 11 that describe testing and affliction.

questions.question: What vow does the psalmist make in Psalms 66:13 after experiencing God's deliverance?
options: To go into God's house with burnt offerings and pay vows
To forget the trials and move on silently
To boast in his own strength
questions.correctAnswer: To go into God's house with burnt offerings and pay vows
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:13 expresses the psalmist’s commitment to worship God through burnt offerings and fulfilling vows, showing gratitude after deliverance, which connects to the previous verses about trials and deliverance.

questions.question: In Psalms 66:14, what prompts the psalmist to offer vows and burnt offerings?
options: The troubles he experienced and the words his lips and mouth uttered
A feeling of superiority over others
questions.correctAnswer: The troubles he experienced and the words his lips and mouth uttered
questions.explanation: Verse 14 explains that the psalmist’s vows and offerings stem from the distress he faced and his spoken prayers, reflecting sincere devotion as a response to God’s help, related to verses 13 and 12.

questions.question: How does Psalms 66:8-10 teach us about responding to God’s testing and sustaining power in Christian living?
options: By praising God, recognizing His sustaining care, and accepting His testing as refining
By ignoring God's testing and focusing on human strength
By blaming God for hardships without praise
By avoiding trials through worldly means
questions.correctAnswer: By praising God, recognizing His sustaining care, and accepting His testing as refining
questions.explanation: Verses 8 to 10 together instruct believers to bless God and praise Him for holding them in life and refining them through trials, teaching faith and trust during hardships.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is emphasized by the psalmist’s commitment in Psalms 66:13-15?
options: Faithfulness in fulfilling vows and grateful worship
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness in fulfilling vows and grateful worship
questions.explanation: Verses 13 to 15 show the psalmist’s dedication to honor God with sacrifices and vows, illustrating faithfulness and gratitude as key Christian virtues.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:12 teach about God’s deliverance despite severe trials?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that although the people went through fire and water (severe trials), God brought them out into a wealthy place, affirming God's power to deliver.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 66:11-12, what biblical truth applies to a believer facing overwhelming hardships?
options: God may allow affliction but ultimately delivers to a prosperous place
Hardships mean God has abandoned them
Deliverance depends solely on personal strength
questions.correctAnswer: God may allow affliction but ultimately delivers to a prosperous place
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 teach that although God allows trials (net, affliction, fire, water), He also brings His people to a wealthy place, offering hope and trust in His deliverance.

questions.question: What is the significance of the psalmist’s words in Psalms 66:14 regarding his vows and songs spoken in trouble?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 14 shows the psalmist’s vocal prayers and vows made during trouble, emphasizing integrity and sincerity in prayer as essential for Christian living.

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:9-10, how should believers view God’s trials in their lives?
options: As a refining process to prove and purify them
questions.correctAnswer: As a refining process to prove and purify them
questions.explanation: These verses describe God holding life and trying believers as silver is tried, teaching that trials are purposeful and purifying rather than arbitrary or punitive.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:13-14 reveal about the relationship between prayer, vows, and worship?
options: Prayer in trouble leads to vows which result in worship with offerings
Vows are made independently of prayer and worship
Worship is only for joyful times, not trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer in trouble leads to vows which result in worship with offerings
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 show the psalmist’s vows and offerings flow from prayers spoken during trouble, highlighting the connection between prayer, commitment, and worship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:11 teach about God's role in the afflictions believers face?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states 'Thou broughtest us into the net; thou laidst affliction upon our loins,' indicating God allows affliction, not that He is absent. The answer is false if one thinks God is not involved in affliction.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 66 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 66.

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:15, which animals are mentioned as burnt offerings?
questions.correctAnswer: Fatlings, rams, bullocks, and goats
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:15 explicitly states the burnt sacrifices of fatlings, with the incense of rams, bullocks, and goats are offered.

questions.question: What invitation does the psalmist extend in Psalms 66:16?
options: Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what He hath done for my soul
Sing aloud unto God, all ye lands
Bless the Lord, all ye people
Rejoice in the Lord, all ye nations
questions.correctAnswer: Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what He hath done for my soul
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:16 invites all who fear God to listen as the psalmist declares God's works for his soul.

questions.question: In Psalms 66:17, how did the psalmist express his cry to God?
questions.correctAnswer: With his mouth and tongue
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:17 says the psalmist cried unto God with his mouth and extolled Him with his tongue.

questions.question: What condition does Psalms 66:18 state affects the Lord's hearing of prayers?
options: If iniquity is regarded in the heart
If the prayer is made at night
If the prayer is spoken in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: If iniquity is regarded in the heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:18 warns that the Lord will not hear if iniquity is cherished in the heart.

questions.question: What assurance does the psalmist give in Psalms 66:19 about God’s response?
options: God has heard and attended to the voice of my prayer
God is silent in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: God has heard and attended to the voice of my prayer
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:19 affirms that God has indeed heard and paid attention to the psalmist’s prayer.

questions.question: How does Psalms 66:20 describe God’s mercy toward the psalmist?
options: God has not turned away my prayer nor His mercy from me
questions.correctAnswer: God has not turned away my prayer nor His mercy from me
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:20 gives praise because God has neither rejected the psalmist’s prayer nor withheld mercy.

questions.question: Which verse in Psalms 66 mentions the testing of the people as silver is tried, symbolizing purification?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalms 66:10
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:10 uses the simile of silver being tried to describe God’s testing of His people.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the repetition of 'Come and' in Psalms 66:5 and Psalms 66:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The repeated invitation 'Come and' at Psalms 66:5 and 66:16 frames the section, creating an inclusio that highlights the call to witness God's works.

questions.question: The phrase 'He turned the sea into dry land' in Psalms 66:6 alludes to which Old Testament event?
options: The parting of the Red Sea during the Exodus
The crossing of the Jordan River into Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: The parting of the Red Sea during the Exodus
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:6 references God's power in making the sea dry, which echoes the Exodus event where Israel crossed the Red Sea on dry ground (Exodus 14:21-22).

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of God hearing sincere prayer despite human frailty, as expressed in Psalms 66:19?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 John 5:14
questions.explanation: 1 John 5:14 states that if we ask anything according to God's will, He hears us, aligning with Psalms 66:19’s assurance that God listens to sincere prayers.

questions.question: In the cultural context of ancient Israel, what was the significance of offering 'burnt sacrifices of fatlings' as mentioned in Psalms 66:15?
options: It was a costly offering signifying dedication and thanksgiving
It was a common, everyday meal offering
It was an offering only for kings
It symbolized sin and guilt without forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: It was a costly offering signifying dedication and thanksgiving
questions.explanation: Burnt offerings of fatlings were valuable, symbolizing full dedication and gratitude to God, reflecting the psalmist’s deep reverence (Psalms 66:15).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'Selah' (e.g., in Psalms 66:4, 7, 15) most likely indicate in the Psalm?
options: A pause for contemplation or musical interlude
A name of a musical instrument
A call to fast and pray
questions.correctAnswer: A pause for contemplation or musical interlude
questions.explanation: The word 'Selah' is widely understood as a liturgical pause or musical interlude, inviting the reader or listener to reflect, as seen in Psalms 66:4, 7, and 15.

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:12, through what hardships did God bring the people, and what was the outcome?
options: Through fire and water, but brought them to a wealthy place
Through famine and war, but brought them to peace
Through exile and captivity, but brought them to freedom
Through darkness and shadow, but brought them to light
questions.correctAnswer: Through fire and water, but brought them to a wealthy place
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:12 describes the people passing through severe trials like fire and water, yet God delivered them into prosperity.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 66:18 teaches that God will always hear prayers regardless of the state of one’s heart.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:18 clearly states that if iniquity is regarded in the heart, the Lord will not hear the person’s prayer.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 66:9 expresses confidence that God sustains life and keeps one’s footing stable.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:9 says God holds the soul in life and does not allow the feet to be moved, showing divine sustenance and stability.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 66 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 66 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily demonstrated in Psalms 66:3 by the phrase 'How terrible art thou in thy works!'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's omnipotence
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:3 highlights God's terrifying power in His works, showing His supreme omnipotence as even His enemies submit to Him.

questions.question: What theological truth is conveyed by Psalms 66:7 stating 'He ruleth by his power for ever; his eyes behold the nations'?
options: God is sovereign over all nations eternally
God is limited to Israel only
God is unaware of human affairs
God relinquishes control to human rulers
questions.correctAnswer: God is sovereign over all nations eternally
questions.explanation: Verse 7 teaches God's eternal sovereignty and vigilant oversight over all nations, affirming His universal reign.

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:10, what does the testing of the people by God resemble?
questions.correctAnswer: The trying of silver
questions.explanation: Psalms 66:10 explicitly compares God's testing of His people to the refining process of silver, illustrating purification through trial.

questions.question: How does Psalms 66:11 describe the nature of affliction experienced by the faithful?
options: As a net and affliction upon the loins
questions.correctAnswer: As a net and affliction upon the loins
questions.explanation: Verse 11 metaphorically portrays affliction as a trapping net and burden on the loins, highlighting the severity of trials.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:12 teach about God's deliverance after severe trials?
options: God abandons His people in fire and water
God brings His people into a wealthy place after trials
questions.correctAnswer: God brings His people into a wealthy place after trials
questions.explanation: This verse affirms that although believers pass through intense trials ('fire and water'), God ultimately brings them into blessing and abundance.

questions.question: What doctrinal theme is expressed in Psalms 66:18 concerning iniquity and prayer?
options: God does not hear prayers when iniquity is regarded in the heart
Iniquity increases the power of prayer
questions.correctAnswer: God does not hear prayers when iniquity is regarded in the heart
questions.explanation: Verse 18 teaches the doctrine of holiness in prayer, indicating that harboring sin hinders God's hearing of prayer.

questions.question: According to Psalms 66:9, which attribute of God is emphasized by 'Which holdeth our soul in life, and suffereth not our feet to be moved'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's protection and sustaining power
questions.explanation: This verse reveals God's sustaining care and protection, preserving life and stability even amid trials.

questions.question: How does Psalms 66:6's description of God turning the sea into dry land relate to the broader biblical narrative?
options: It foreshadows the resurrection of Christ
It recalls the Exodus deliverance of Israel
It predicts the destruction of Babylon
It symbolizes the creation of the world
questions.correctAnswer: It recalls the Exodus deliverance of Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 6 alludes to God's mighty act in the Exodus, a foundational redemptive event foreshadowing salvation.

questions.question: What does the combined teaching of Psalms 66:13-15 reveal about the proper response to God's deliverance?
options: Offering vows and sacrifices of thanksgiving
questions.correctAnswer: Offering vows and sacrifices of thanksgiving
questions.explanation: Verses 13-15 reveal that God's deliverance calls for a response of worship through vows, burnt offerings, and praise.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Psalms 66:16 and 66:19 provide about prayer and divine response?
options: God hears and attends to the prayers of those who fear Him
Prayer is ineffective regardless of faith
God only hears prayers of the righteous without faults
questions.correctAnswer: God hears and attends to the prayers of those who fear Him
questions.explanation: Together these verses affirm that God actively hears and responds to the prayers of the faithful who fear Him.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine justice is inconsistent because the faithful suffer hardship. What does Psalms 66:10-12 actually teach about God's justice and providence?
options: God tests His people through trials but ultimately delivers them to prosperity
God abandons His people in suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God tests His people through trials but ultimately delivers them to prosperity
questions.explanation: These verses teach that God’s justice includes refining trials and assured deliverance, showing providence rather than neglect.

questions.question: What aspect of God's nature is emphasized by the exhortation in Psalms 66:8 'O bless our God, ye people, and make the voice of his praise to be heard'?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s worthiness of universal worship
questions.explanation: Verse 8 emphasizes God’s intrinsic worthiness to be praised universally, reflecting His glory and honor.

questions.question: What does Psalms 66:17 reveal about the believer’s response to God in times of distress?
options: The believer cries out and extols God with the tongue
questions.correctAnswer: The believer cries out and extols God with the tongue
questions.explanation: This verse shows that the faithful respond to trouble by calling on God verbally and giving Him praise.

questions.question: How do Psalms 66:4 and 66:8 together contribute to the biblical theology of worship?
options: They emphasize exclusive worship of Israel only
They affirm that all the earth and all people are called to praise God
They teach that worship is optional
questions.correctAnswer: They affirm that all the earth and all people are called to praise God
questions.explanation: Verse 4 calls all the earth to sing and worship God, and verse 8 commands all people to bless God, showing universal worship.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is taught by the description in Psalms 66:20 that God 'hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me'?
options: The doctrine of divine mercy and faithfulness to prayer
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine mercy and faithfulness to prayer
questions.explanation: This verse affirms God's mercy and faithfulness in answering prayer, foundational to the doctrine of grace.
